The Bill

One magician, three very different rooms.

Eric reads a room fast and adjusts — the slapstick a six-year-old loves isn't the same show a boardroom gets. Here's how the act shifts to fit the crowd.

♣
For the Office

Corporate & Holiday Parties

Strolling close-up magic for the first hour before the meal — the fastest icebreaker in the business. Barkley Advertising has booked Eric 8 years running for exactly this reason: it gets a room full of coworkers actually talking to each other.

♥
For the Occasion

Bachelorettes & House Parties

Living room, kitchen island, folding chairs — doesn't matter. Eric turns whatever space you've got into a stage, gets everyone off their phones, and leaves the group with a story they'll retell for years.

♦
For the Family

Birthdays, Ages 4 and Up

Four-year-olds and fourteen-year-olds don't laugh at the same things, and Eric's spent years learning the difference — slapstick and silliness for the little ones, real audience participation and a bit of danger once they're older.

Organically ranked #1 comedy magician in Kansas City for over a decade
The Man Behind the Cards

A magician who trained for the room, not just the trick.

The Training

After earning his degree at KU, Eric trained at The Second City Improv School — the same room that's shaped some of comedy's sharpest improvisers. It's why his shows feel less like a script and more like a conversation: quick, spontaneous, and built around whoever happens to be standing in front of him that night.

The Instinct

Twenty-six years ago, Eric started Magic At Hand and organically climbed to the #1 spot in Kansas City — and held it for over a decade. Years in medical sales sharpened something most magicians never bother learning: how to read a client fast, put them at ease, and communicate like a person instead of a performer.

The Result

Clean comedy, strong original magic, and a smile that's apparently contagious enough to get mentioned in almost every single review. Age-appropriate for a six-year-old's birthday, sharp enough for a glitzy corporate stage, and everything in between.

Fun Fact

Eric once got flagged down mid-bike-ride by Tom Shadyac — the director behind Ace Ventura, Liar Liar, and Bruce Almighty. Which feels a little on-the-nose, since half of Eric's audiences already swear he's a dead ringer for Shadyac's favorite leading man, Jim Carrey.
